card.name: Entire or whole before plural places
card.fires_on: The word entire or whole (or the plural noun right after it) when it quantifies large groups or places, such as countries, populations, towns or areas, especially in descriptions of destruction.

modes.label: Entire/whole before a plural
modes.description: The word entire or whole used before a plural noun for places or groups affected by destruction.
modes.example: The twister killed six people and destroyed<< entire>> swaths of the North Texas town.

modes.label: Plural noun after entire
modes.description: The plural noun that follows entire or whole, such as countries or quarters.
modes.example: This is more than the known oil reserves of entire<< countries>> that the U.S. currently imports oil

card.writes: It pushes the model toward plural collective nouns like scenarios, projects, programs and campaigns.
card.plain: It marks words like "entire" or "whole" that sit before plural nouns for large groups or places, such as countries or towns.
